name: GitHub
description: Connect GitHub to search repositories and code, manage files and issues, create and review pull requests, and query users and teams.
authorization.title: Authorize a GitHub account
authorization.description: Enter a GitHub personal access token (PAT) in the POCO authorization form. Accessible repositories and operations depend on the token's permissions and organization policies.
authorization.token.label: GitHub personal access token
authorization.token.description: Go to GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens. Select the target repositories and permissions needed for your operations when creating the token.
authorization.token.placeholder: Enter a GitHub personal access token
configuration.endpoint.label: MCP endpoint
configuration.endpoint.description: The official GitHub remote MCP endpoint for the default toolsets. Keep the default value.
capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.repos.title: Repositories and code
capabilities.repos.description: Search repositories and code; read files, commits, branches, tags, and releases; create, fork, or delete repositories and commit file changes.
capabilities.issues.title: Issue management
capabilities.issues.description: Read and maintain issues, labels, fields, and sub-issue relationships; add comments or reactions.
capabilities.pullRequests.title: Pull request collaboration
capabilities.pullRequests.description: Read pull request diffs, comments, and check status; create or update pull requests, submit reviews, update branches, and merge pull requests.
capabilities.users.title: Users and teams
capabilities.users.description: Read the current user, teams, and team members; search users and list repository collaborators.
limits.title: Usage limits
limits.description: Only tools allowed by this connector and returned by the remote service are available. Writes such as file commits, comments, reviews, merges, and deletions require confirmation. After a timeout, check the result before submitting again.
examples.title: Examples
examples.search.title: Locate an implementation
examples.search.description: Find login-related code in a specified GitHub repository and explain the main call relationships.
examples.issues.title: Summarize open issues
examples.issues.description: List open bug issues in a specified repository, including titles, assignees, and links.
examples.review.title: Review a pull request
examples.review.description: Read a specified pull request's diff and check results, then identify issues that need attention.
